title: bug: setting an epic to ARCHIVED through moe.update_epic or the board's /ws UPDATE_EPIC (both plugins' epic status combo offers Archived) skips every guard of moe.archive_epic, so in-flight rows keep running under an ARCHIVED epic, its tasks are never archived, and workers can no longer file cards into it
description:
Filed by defect hunt #12 (task-f6f0b580, architect-1dd28c7c). Both hunt lanes found it independently. Reproduced at moe/work-2026-10-24 f159784e; the files are unchanged at cbae6070.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/):
- moe.archive_epic:
  - refuses while any task is PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING (archiveEpic.ts:12, :61);
  - applies archive_task's holder rule to held BLOCKED rows (:15-28);
  - archives every task with a TASK_ARCHIVED event.
- moe.update_epic passes status through without any of those rules: updateEpic.ts:90 `if (params.status !== undefined) updates.status = params.status;` goes to StateManager.updateEpic, whose validateEpicUpdates accepts 'ARCHIVED' (state/validators.ts:587). Its inputSchema enum leaves ARCHIVED out (updateEpic.ts:38), but McpAdapter does not enforce schemas, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md:1908 lists ARCHIVED.
- /ws UPDATE_EPIC (server/WebSocketServer.ts:664-674) hands the plugin's updates straight to state.updateEpic.
  - JetBrains EpicDetailDialog.kt:31 offers ARCHIVED in its status combo, saved via MoeCommandSender.kt:104-118.
  - VS Code EpicDetailPanel.ts:291 offers Archived.
- Effect: only the epic's status flips.
  - In-flight rows keep running.
  - The board snapshot drops the epic but keeps its tasks (WebSocketServer.ts:397-398).
  - create_task into the epic is refused with "Epic is ARCHIVED: … un-archive the epic first" (taskStore.ts:307), so a worker cannot file a bug: card into its own epic.
  - The epic's tasks are never archived, so their dependents are never released.
- Related: the shelved row task-75eae924 called ARCHIVED invalid for update_epic. Since then 68a47060 made ARCHIVED a valid create_epic status. So keep ARCHIVED valid and make it safe; do not refuse it outright.

EVIDENCE (git-archive snapshot of f159784e; my re-runs are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/me/):
- /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/B/zzHuntB_epicArchive.test.ts uses zzHuntB_harness.ts (a real StateManager, McpAdapter and MoeWebSocketServer on an ephemeral port) and sends the exact JetBrains EpicDetailDialog payload. Result: Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3).
  - ✓ twin: archive_epic refuses an epic with an in-flight (WORKING) task and writes nothing
  - × /ws UPDATE_EPIC status ARCHIVED must not archive an epic whose task is in flight → AssertionError: expected { epic: 'ARCHIVED', …(2) } to deeply equal { epic: 'ACTIVE', …(2) }. The task stays WORKING, and a spinoff create_task is refused "Epic is ARCHIVED: epic-1 — un-archive the epic first".
  - × /ws UPDATE_EPIC status ARCHIVED on a quiescent epic must shelve its tasks like archive_epic does → AssertionError: expected 'BACKLOG' to be 'ARCHIVED'
- /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_updateEpicArchive.test.ts (the MCP update_epic path): Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4).
  - × (r1) update_epic status ARCHIVED with a WORKING row is refused and the epic stays live → promise resolved "{ success: true, epic: { …(10) } }" instead of rejecting
  - × (r2) the live row's worker can still file a bug: card into its own epic → promise rejected "Error: Epic is ARCHIVED: epic-1 — un-arch…"
- Exposure: the live board has 0 ARCHIVED epics today (16 ACTIVE, 18 PLANNED, 2 COMPLETED). The plugin path is one combo change plus Save.

FIX DIRECTION: when update_epic or /ws UPDATE_EPIC moves an epic that is not ARCHIVED to ARCHIVED, run archive_epic's semantics instead of a bare status write: the in-flight refusal, the holder rule for a caller with a workerId, and archiving every task.
- For example, delegate to archiveEpicTool(state).handler({ epicId, workerId }), the way /ws RELEASE_TASK delegates to releaseTaskTool, and apply the remaining fields with updateEpic.
- Leave every other status change, and an already-ARCHIVED epic, unchanged.
- The /ws refusal returns as the usual ERROR frame.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/updateEpic.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts (the UPDATE_EPIC case only), optionally packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveEpic.ts (to export a shared helper), and a new test such as src/tools/updateEpic.archive.test.ts.
- Placement: WebSocketServer.ts also holds the WebSocket Origin check (hunt #13's lane) and the UPDATE_SETTINGS case, which the approvalMode row may use. Stay inside the UPDATE_EPIC case; worktree merge-tree lands distinct hunks.
- Sync docs/MCP_SERVER.md's `### moe.update_epic` section only if lanes.js shows that file free at planning time.
definitionOfDone: moe.update_epic { status: 'ARCHIVED' } and /ws UPDATE_EPIC { status: 'ARCHIVED' } on an epic with a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING task are refused (NOT_ALLOWED from the tool, an ERROR frame on /ws) and write nothing: the epic keeps its status and every task is unchanged.

On an epic with no in-flight task, both paths leave the epic ARCHIVED and every task ARCHIVED with a TASK_ARCHIVED event, as moe.archive_epic does, and other fields sent in the same call are still applied.
A new vitest file drives both the MCP handler and a /ws UPDATE_EPIC message and passes, and the existing updateEpic, archiveEpic and WebSocketServer tests stay green.

implementationPlan.description:
The fix. Use your Edit tool.

(a) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/updateEpic.ts
- Change the type import to `import type { Epic, EpicStatus } from '../types/schema.js';`.
- Add `import { validateEpicUpdates } from '../state/validators.js';` and `import { archiveEpicTool } from './archiveEpic.js';`.
- Directly above `export function updateEpicTool`, add:
```ts
/**
 * The one epic-update path of moe.update_epic and the board's /ws UPDATE_EPIC.
 * Moving an epic that is not ARCHIVED yet to ARCHIVED runs moe.archive_epic
 * instead of a bare status write: its in-flight refusal, its holder rule for a
 * caller with a workerId, its finalizing hold, and every task archived with a
 * TASK_ARCHIVED event. The call's other fields are validated before any write
 * and applied after the archive. Every other update, an already-ARCHIVED epic
 * included, stays a plain state.updateEpic.
 */
export async function applyEpicUpdate(
  state: StateManager,
  epicId: string,
  updates: Record<string, unknown>,
  workerId?: string
): Promise<Epic> {
  const epic = state.getEpic(epicId);
  if (!epic || updates?.status !== 'ARCHIVED' || epic.status === 'ARCHIVED') {
    return state.updateEpic(epicId, updates as Partial<Epic>, workerId);
  }
  const { status: _archived, ...rest } = updates;
  const hasRest = Object.keys(rest).length > 0;
  if (hasRest) validateEpicUpdates(rest as Partial<Epic>); // a bad companion field is refused before any write
  await archiveEpicTool(state).handler(workerId === undefined ? { epicId } : { epicId, workerId }, state);
  return hasRest ? state.updateEpic(epicId, rest as Partial<Epic>, workerId) : state.getEpic(epicId)!;
}
```
- In updateEpicTool:
  - The handler's write becomes `const epic = await applyEpicUpdate(state, params.epicId, updates, workerId as string | undefined);`. The allowed-field check and assertDesignatable still run first, unchanged.
  - The description becomes `'Update an existing epic. status ARCHIVED on an epic that is not archived yet runs moe.archive_epic first (refused while any task is PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING, or, for a caller with a workerId, while another worker holds a BLOCKED task; otherwise every task is archived), then applies the other fields.'`.
  - The status schema becomes `{ type: 'string', enum: ['PLANNED', 'ACTIVE', 'COMPLETED', 'ARCHIVED'], description: 'Epic status. ARCHIVED follows moe.archive_epic (see the tool description).' }`. This is additive: validateEpicUpdates already accepted ARCHIVED, and the reply shape `{ success, epic }` is unchanged.

(b) packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts. Touch only two places: the import list and the `case 'UPDATE_EPIC'` body.
- Add `import { applyEpicUpdate } from '../tools/updateEpic.js';` right after `import { releaseTaskTool } from '../tools/releaseTask.js';`.
- In UPDATE_EPIC, replace `const epic = await this.withMutex(() => this.state.updateEpic(epicId, updates as Record<string, unknown>));` with these two comment lines and the new call:
  `// moe.update_epic's path: a move to ARCHIVED follows moe.archive_epic`
  `// (in-flight refusal, every task archived); a refusal is the ERROR frame.`
  `const epic = await this.withMutex(() => applyEpicUpdate(this.state, epicId, updates as Record<string, unknown>));`
- Leave the EPIC_UPDATED reply, the Origin check, UPDATE_SETTINGS and every other case alone. Other lanes edit them, and merge-tree lands distinct hunks.
- The board call carries no workerId, so it is a human for the holder rule, exactly as archive_epic treats a caller-less call.

Error handling:
- Every refusal is thrown before the first write: an invalid companion field from validateEpicUpdates, then archive_epic's NOT_ALLOWED in-flight and holder gates, then its finalizing-hold refusal.
- The MCP path returns the coded error. /ws turns it into the existing catch-all ERROR frame `{ type: 'ERROR', message, operation: 'UPDATE_EPIC', code, codeName, context }`, so no new error path is added.
- A missing epic or a non-object `updates` keeps today's plain-path errors (`Epic not found`, `updates must be an object`).
- A write failure partway through archiving behaves as archive_epic does today.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review (load adversarial-self-review) of your `git diff`. Fix any finding, then re-run step 3's gates.

(1) Scope: exactly 3 files.
- updateEpic.ts: the imports, applyEpicUpdate, the handler call, the description and the enum.
- WebSocketServer.ts: one import and the UPDATE_EPIC call plus its two comment lines.
- The new test file.

(2) Nothing is written before a refusal. Validation and archive_epic's gates all run before the first updateTask or updateEpic. The companion fields are written only after a successful archive, so a refused call leaves the epic and task files byte-identical ((m1), (m3), (m5), (w1)).

(3) Twice concurrently: MCP dispatch and the /ws handler both hold the reentrant state mutex for the whole call, so gates and writes cannot interleave with another mutation. applyEpicUpdate is never called outside it; check that there is no third caller.

(4) Inputs:
- `updates` undefined, or a non-object from a malformed /ws frame, takes the plain path and its existing error.
- A lowercase 'archived' fails validateEpicUpdates's enum on the plain path, as before.
- A status ARCHIVED with no other fields returns the archived epic.
- An already-ARCHIVED epic, an un-archive (ARCHIVED to ACTIVE) and other status moves are byte-for-byte today's path.

(5) The contract stays additive: the update_epic reply `{ success, epic }` and the EPIC_UPDATED frame keep their shapes. A companion-field call now emits two EPIC_UPDATED activity events (the status, then the fields), plus one TASK_ARCHIVED per task. That is acceptable, so say it in the summary.

(6) Follow-up, out of scope (MCP_SERVER.md was held by dd1e00f8 at planning time, and the DoD allowed the docs edit only if the file was free): the `### moe.update_epic` section should say that ARCHIVED follows moe.archive_epic. Say so in the completion summary.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.update_epic and the board's /ws UPDATE_EPIC share one path, applyEpicUpdate in tools/updateEpic.ts. A move to ARCHIVED of an epic that is not ARCHIVED yet runs moe.archive_epic's semantics instead of a bare status write: it is refused (NOT_ALLOWED) while any task is PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING, or, for a caller with a workerId, while another worker holds a BLOCKED task, and nothing is written. Otherwise every task becomes ARCHIVED with a TASK_ARCHIVED event, the epic becomes ARCHIVED, and the call's other fields (validated before any write) are applied. Every other update, an already-ARCHIVED epic included, is a plain state.updateEpic as before. /ws refusals come back as the usual ERROR frame.
acceptanceCriteria: DoD 1: update_epic {status:'ARCHIVED'} with a PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING task rejects with codeName NOT_ALLOWED, and /ws UPDATE_EPIC answers {type:'ERROR', operation:'UPDATE_EPIC', codeName:'NOT_ALLOWED'}. In both cases the epic and task files stay byte-identical and no TASK_ARCHIVED is logged.
DoD 2: on a quiescent epic both paths leave the epic ARCHIVED with the companion title/description applied, and every task ARCHIVED, with one TASK_ARCHIVED per newly archived task.

DoD 3: the new updateEpic.archive.test.ts (m1-m5, w1-w2) passes, the full daemon suite passes from a whole-tree snapshot (GREEN checkRef), and the new file gives exactly 7 failed | 2 passed (9) against f8b8d60c's sources (RED checkRef).
invariants: No write happens before a refusal. That covers companion-field validation, the in-flight gate, the holder gate and the finalizing hold.
Already-ARCHIVED epics, un-archives and every non-ARCHIVED status move behave exactly as today.
Reply shapes are unchanged: update_epic returns { success, epic } and /ws sends EPIC_UPDATED with the epic payload.
compatibility: update_epic's status enum gains ARCHIVED, which is additive: validateEpicUpdates already accepted it, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md already lists it. The plugins need no change: their Archived combo now gets archive_epic semantics or an ERROR frame.
Existing .moe epics and tasks load unchanged. An epic archived before this fix is left alone.
